cells.tense: You are here in the room, and the feeling moving between you and another person is landing as it should.
cells.ask: Tell someone what their situation stirred in you, once, without adding what they should do about it.
cells.core:
Somebody tells you something hard and it lands in you. You feel the shape of their situation without becoming it, and you stay someone separate while it moves through. That is what makes it worth talking to you.

You are not managing your face or waiting to speak. The feeling arrives, you let it arrive, and it doesn't need to be announced or acted on. You have gotten good at holding something that size without setting it down on the other person. The work now is not to reach harder, it is to keep letting the contact be what it is. Stay in it.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel for someone and stay your own size.
cells.verb: Feeling with another person while staying your own size
cells.place: Where you put down what you have been gripping

cells.tense: You are already carrying what other people might feel before they have had a chance to feel it themselves.
cells.ask: Pick one worry you are holding for someone else and say, out loud, that it is theirs to carry.
cells.core:
Someone mentions a problem and it becomes yours before they finish the sentence. You are already in their future, already solving what hasn't happened, already holding a weight that was theirs to pick up or put down. The feeling is real. The reach is too far.

Where their worry stops and your day starts has gone blurry, and that is what is costing you. When you take on what they haven't handed you, the two of you get less room, not more, and you get tired holding things nobody asked you to hold. Nothing has to end here. Just put one of those loads back where it came from.
cells.sheetLine: You are carrying things that were never handed to you.

cells.tense: You stopped letting things reach you some way back, and you are still standing in the habit.
cells.ask: Ask one person one real question about their week, then listen to the whole answer without filling the quiet.
cells.core:
The ordinary version is close and unremarkable: someone says something true and it lands, you stay in the room with them, you say the thing back that shows you heard it. Two people, one conversation, both of them actually there.

For you the exchanges have stayed on the surface, and you have gotten used to that as just how it goes. It keeps things simple. It also keeps you out of the room. There is no numbness to push through and no feeling to force. What has gone quiet comes back by the small door, one ordinary exchange at a time. Nothing was lost. It went unused. Give it one plain conversation and see what comes.
cells.sheetLine: The connection is still there, just out of practice.

cells.tense: You are already picking up what people need and you call it nothing, because noticing doesn't count as giving.
cells.ask: Name one thing you did today that was for someone else, and this time let it count as care.
cells.core:
You are the one people call when something has gone wrong, and you show up. You answer the late message, you remember what someone is dealing with, you handle things quietly so nobody has to ask twice. None of that reads as warmth to you. It reads as being practical, or just doing what needs doing.

Nothing about this is hidden from anyone but you. What you call indifference is showing on the outside the whole time, in the calls you take and the small things you keep track of, and you keep filing it under something else. The care keeps moving. Only your account of it has gone quiet.
cells.sheetLine: What you call nothing is care, and people feel it.

attempts.check: The record says others feel your compassion while you feel nothing; it does not say they actually name this to you, and my draft should not put that claim in their mouth. A reader could reasonably say they are simply private, or that they have deliberately stopped reaching for people rather than lost anything. The ask survives being wrong because speaking one plain sentence about someone's day asks nothing of their feelings in return, and they would still have named something real. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line about others feeling warmth they never return — cut it, and leave what I can see.
